raw_response:
At 65, with 40 years on these same 4.5 mu, I know this ground well. My wife and I manage it ourselves — the kids are working in town, they come back only at busy times. With my high school agricultural training I still read the extension bulletins, and I had my soil tested two years back: medium fertility, organic matter a bit low, pH around 7.8. I farm carefully because on 4.5 mu every yuan of input has to earn itself back, but I can't afford a yield failure either — we depend on this grain for our own eating plus some cash.

**Wheat (2.5 mu in the wheat-maize fields; all 4.5 mu actually since it's double cropping):**
I'll plant around October 12-15, which is when my neighbors plant and what the experience tells me works here. Jimai 22 variety — it's been steady for me, resists lodging, handles our dry springs. Seeding rate 15 kg/mu, a bit on the heavier side because I plant later than ideal. Before planting I'll broadcast 40 kg/mu of 15-15-15 compound as base, that's 6 kg each N, P, K. At jointing, late March, I topdress 15 kg urea per mu — another 7 kg N. Total N about 13 kg/mu. I used to apply more when I was younger but I've learned this land doesn't respond above 14-15 — and urea prices haven't come down.

Irrigation — pre-winter if November is dry, then jointing, heading, grain fill. Three times most years, four if spring drought. The pump meter doesn't lie, so I watch rain carefully before turning it on.

**Maize (same 4.5 mu, right after wheat):**
Harvest wheat around June 8-10, then I have maybe 5 days to get maize planted. Zhengdan 958 hybrid, about 2 kg seed/mu. I hire the no-till planter — I can't run that machine at my age, and it places fertilizer with the seed so I save a pass. Base compound fertilizer 30 kg/mu plus urea 10 kg at planting, then 20 kg urea side-dressed at big-trumpet stage (V10-12). N total around 14 kg/mu. Maize irrigation — usually 1-2 times, depends on July-August rainfall. If there's a good rain pattern I skip it.

**Pesticides:** Pre-emergence herbicide on wheat (isoproturon), post-emergence atrazine on maize. I scout for aphids on wheat around heading — if I see them I spray, if not I save the money. Corn borer usually shows up; I'll use a dust or a single spray.

**Labor:** Mostly me and my wife, about 25 person-days each across both crops. I hire the combine for wheat harvest, planter for maize, and combine for maize — roughly 80 yuan/mu for the machine services across the year. At my age, there's no doing it by hand anymore.

decision.reasoning_summary: At my age and on only 4.5 mu, I'm not chasing maximum yield — I'm managing for steady, reliable returns on land I know intimately. My soil test two years ago showed medium fertility, so I keep N around 13-14 kg/mu on both crops, which my experience says is where this ground responds without waste. I split fertilizer on both crops to match crop demand. I rely on hired machinery for tillage, planting, and harvest because my wife and I can't handle that work anymore, and I irrigate conservatively because the electric pump runs up the bill fast. The wheat-maize rotation has worked here for decades and I see no reason to change it.
